correctness.rationale: The proof independently establishes the complete two-level vertex set. A pair distance is an exact rational function of two subset sizes and their overlap; the overlap coefficient is strictly negative. After minimizing overlap, both chambers are strictly decreasing in squared imbalance. Their balanced envelopes are monotone to the half-size boundary, and a strict rational comparison controls the odd-N integral gap. Strict squared-distance convexity excludes all nonvertex extremal points. An independent exact-arithmetic program verified all feasible cardinality/intersection orbits \(2\le N\le50\) and all explicit vertex pairs \(2\le N\le9\) (506298 assertions). The finite program is corroboration, not proof of the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The trisection central polytopes form an intrinsic classical geometric family with exponentially many vertices and a known closed volume ratio. The complete Euclidean diameter graph is a genuinely different extremal invariant not determined by vertex count, volume, or affine combinatorics. The result shows the extreme graph collapses to a matching supported only on one or two central vertex layers, and gives sharp dimension parity, multiplicities, and an exact strict odd-dimensional deficit. This natural full classification has a nontrivial global overlap/balance proof and applies in arbitrarily high dimension.
